text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The newspaper editorial said it was dangerous to politicise and limit crime by always blaming the ex-communist secret police. The authorities should tackle state corruption.
- People living in a wrecked building wrecked by an explosion said they were terrified. They also complained that police took control of their apartments.
- Azem Hajdari, a ruling party MP, clashed with the head of the independent trade union Valer Xheka on the union presidency.
- All political parties oppose a parliamentary committee drawing up the new constitution, as the ruling party says.
- Albanian rural families lack modern technology to work in their land property.
- The Albanian lek became significantly strong on Wednesday reaching an exchange rate of below 100 leks per dollar.
- Italian police have blocked hundreds of illegal Albanian immigrants and 114 kg of marijuana transported with powerful speedboats from the Balkan country to neighbouring Italy.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha congratulates Bill Clinton for his re-election and Boris Yeltsin for a speedy recovery after his operation.
- Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his deputy and Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu will participate in the Central European Initiative meeting in Graz, Austria.
- Ibrahim Rugova, leader of the ethnic Albanians in the Yugoslav province of Kosovo, congratulates Clinton for his re-election.
- Fatos Nano, the jailed leader of the opposition Socialist Party, sends best wishes to Clinton for his presidential victory.
